extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: The largest open dataset for language model pre-training containing about two trillion tokens of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data. The dataset includes a wide variety of languages from main European languages to low-resource ones, plus a large portion of code data, covering diverse domains and time periods.
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Arnett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus aggregates data from multiple sources including digitized books and newspapers from national libraries, government documents, open source code repositories, scientific publications, and web content. Data was collected through various methods including API access, entire database dumps, web scraping, and reuse of existing digitized collections. Major collection-as-data initiatives include Chronicle America (Library of Congress newspapers), Europeana (European newspapers), Gallica (French National Library), and various other national library digitization projects.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of digitized books, newspapers, and periodicals from national libraries and archives; government documents from agencies like USPTO, UN, OECD, and EU institutions; open source code; scientific publications; and web content. Sources include public domain and permissively licensed materials such as US PD Books (140,000 books), US PD Newspapers (21 million newspapers), French PD Books (289,000 books), French PD Newspapers (3 million editions), Europeana Newspapers (1,000+ newspapers from 23 libraries), and various other national collections.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Historical content spans from 1618 to 2022, with most cultural heritage materials (books and newspapers) published between 1690-1990. Government documents include USPTO data from 2019-2022. The dataset compilation itself was an ongoing effort since 2024.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext for text segmentation; OCRoscope and OCRerrcr for OCR error detection; OCRonos (Llama 3 8B-based) for OCR correction; Microsoft's Presidio for PII identification; Celadon (DeBERTa-v3-small) for toxicity classification; fastText for language identification
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains historical content from newspapers and books spanning 1618-2000, which may reflect historical biases and perspectives of those time periods. OCR errors from digitized historical documents are present. The coverage for low-resource languages is shallow, with disproportionate representation of European languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data (the 'open data paradox'). The 2 trillion tokens are suitable for pre-training models of limited size, but larger models will require significantly more data. The dataset does not contain data for instruction-tuning or specialized tasks, making it unsuitable for task-specific fine-tuning. Curation methods cannot facilitate hundred-percent accuracy. Coverage for low-resource languages is shallow, particularly for African languages.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus addresses legal and regulatory concerns in AI development by providing truly open pre-training data compliant with data security regulations, particularly EU AI regulations. It enables open LLM research while meeting legal requirements, avoiding copyright infringement issues that have plagued other datasets. The dataset supports multilingual AI development beyond English, promoting linguistic diversity. It serves as critical infrastructure for open science research in LLMs.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset underwent PII (Personally Identifiable Information) removal as part of the curation process. Historical newspapers and books may contain references to individuals, but PII mitigation was applied during data processing.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for pre-training Large Language Models, particularly models of limited to medium size. It has been used by industry leaders like Anthropic and multiple LLM training projects. The dataset is suitable for creating ethical fine-tuning datasets for specialized applications like RAG models. Due to multilingual, temporal, and semantic diversity, it opens opportunities for diverse research and entrepreneurial needs.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is an ongoing effort that started in 2024 and has grown to 2 trillion tokens. The team is currently collecting more data in European languages as part of the LLMs4EU project and planning enlargement of corpora in African languages (e.g., Swahili, Wolof, Bambara). Each data object is accompanied by sufficient metadata. The dataset is maintained with support from AI Alliance, LANGU:IA, French Ministry of Culture, and various partner organizations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The Open Culture data in Common Corpus have been post-processed and filtered, which results in a slightly different final word and token count from the original collections. Data sources were dispatched into smaller individual subsets and separately released as parts of the Open Culture collection.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Common Corpus1, the largest open dataset for language model pre-training.

description.evidence: The data assembled in Common Corpus are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses and amount to about two trillion tokens. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the main European languages to low-resource ones rarely present in pre-training datasets; in addition, it includes a large portion of code data.
